h: פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי מוֹת, א׳ Acharei Mos, 1
Faith Opens the Heart to the Holiness of Yom Kippur

p: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ אֶל מֹשֶׁה דַּבֵּר וְגוֹ׳ (שָׁם, ב)
"And Hashem said to Moshe: Speak," etc. (16:2).
it is not mentioned what was spoken,
and why does it say "And He said,"
that is, the attribute of Malchus,
which is also called by the Name Havayah.
is the speech of the Written Torah,
for it is written 'And He spoke,' etc.,
That is, the words of Torah
that are the speech of this parshah
came about through the sons of Aharon;
and this is what it says, "after the death," etc.,
and then the parshah was written through them.
that it is written in the parshah of Yom Kippur,
(סוֹף פָּרָשָׁה כ, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כ, יב)
so why does it mention their death
there came about and was written
that is, saying in a whisper,
where it is not openly recognizable
how it comes from Hashem Yisbarach,
shines into the heart of the Sages,
And this is what was said to Moshe:
the sensing of the light in the heart.
And this is what it says,
בְּזֹאת יָבֹא אַהֲרֹן אֶל הַקּוֹדֶשׁ (שָׁם, ג)
"With this shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary" (16:3);
for the holy Zohar already asked
'and let him not come at all times,'
at what time he should enter?"
Only at the end of the parshah
that "zos" is called the attribute of Malchus;
it is an open revelation to the eye,
where one points with the finger.
will be only in the future,
"In the future the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.,
and each one points with his finger, etc.:
זֶה ה׳ קִוִּינוּ לוֹ וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה כה, ט)
'This is Hashem, for whom we hoped,' etc." (Yeshayahu 25:9).
except at the splitting of the Yam Suf,
as they said (in the Mechilta, Beshalach, Shirah 3,
וְזוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב סד, ב)
וְאָז אָמְרוּ זֶה אֵלִי וְגוֹ׳ (שְׁמוֹת טו, ב)
and then they said, "This is my God," etc. (Shemos 15:2).
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם ס, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 60a):
of the glory of their King was no longer there," etc.
And so at the time of the giving of the Torah
and there is no longer such a revelation
in this world until the future.
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג רל, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (III 230a):
"it is truth and it is faith."
"Just as in your heart there is only One";
that is, in your heart it is open
"so in our heart there is only One":
even though it is not so open
it is open in our heart
"Fortunate is the man who does this,"
and as it is expounded in Midrash Rabbah
(פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, פָּרָשָׁה כא, וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה כא, ו)
"'With this': in the merit of Shabbos," etc.
For Shabbos is a semblance of the World to Come,
"one sixtieth of the World to Come,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 88a):
on Atika Kadisha, on Ze'ir Anpin,
and on the Field of Apples," etc.
for then there is complete faith,
And this is what He told him,
"With this shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary":
that is, when he senses in his heart
then he may come into the Sanctuary.
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar (III 58b):
which is complete faith, as was said.
But on Shabbos the holiness is
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
"to know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you";
only when he senses in his heart
that comes from his own side.
And about this he was told
at the end of the parshah
which is also of the holiness of Shabbos,
and they can bring into it
the holiness of Shabbos from the side of Yisrael.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא
And it too is a semblance of the World to Come,
and it is even more a semblance of the World to Come,
שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ לֹא אֲכִילָה וְלֹא שְׁתִיָּה
for there is no eating or drinking on it,
just like the World to Come itself;
and it is called Shabbas Shabbason,
and it is from the side of Yisrael;
and then he may come into the Sanctuary.
the time when Aharon may come into the Sanctuary:
when he senses such a revelation in his heart;
and this is saying in a whisper,
regarding the plain meaning of the parshah,
that through the sons of Aharon came about
and the service of Yom Kippur.
"and let him not come at all times,"
and as written in the holy Zohar:
וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּתִי לְךָ ה׳ עֵת רָצוֹן
'And as for me, my prayer is to You, Hashem, at a time of favor.'"
And this is according to what they said
(מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה וָאֶתְחַנַּן, דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ב, יב)
but the sea is always open,
כָּךְ יָדוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
so the hand of the Holy One, blessed be He,
קְרִיבִין לְגַבֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא כוּ׳
they draw close to the Holy One, blessed be He, etc.;
with greater will of the heart," etc.
and they merit the fiftieth gate,
which is the World to Come.
But the Kohen Gadol He warned,
"and let him not come at all times."
when there is a joining of "time,"
which is the attribute of Malchus,
which is the will of Atika
which is the crown of Malchus;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קנו, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (II 156a):
this too is a combination together;
they are included in one another
And this joining is on Shabbos,
Ze'ir Anpin and the Field of Apples.
it is from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
אָז בְּזֹאת יָבֹא אַהֲרֹן אֶל הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
then "with this shall Aharon come into the Sanctuary."
And this is what was revealed to Moshe Rabbeinu
it is what it says, "With this shall he come."

paragraphs.text: Source: Devarim Rabbah 2:12 — “… רחוקים, מה המקוה הזה פעמים פתוח פעמים נעול, אף שערי תפלה פעמים פתוחים פעמים נעולים, אבל הים הזה לעולם פתוח, כך ידו של הקדוש ברוך הוא לעולם פתוחה לקבל שבים. …” — “Another matter: “As is the Lord our God” – this is what the verse said: “But as for me, let my prayer come to You, Lord, at a time of favor” (Psalms 69:14). Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa asked Rabbi Shmuel …”
